owner_visual.note: Plan Conformance row O03 (S3): docs/evidence/S3/owner/ — download progress, checksum failure, fallback banner (plus ready and still-works shots), captured from a passing run; gallery.md links them; the tick-list is posted in issue #56 for the owner.

limitations: The runtime+model pair is resolved by MEASUREMENT in S4 (plan D5); S3 pins the smallest plausible candidate (Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M, Apache-2.0, 396,705,472 bytes) and the manager is format-agnostic machinery — S4 may re-pin after its measurement.

The model cache backend is selected at runtime by a real probe: OPFS on Chromium, Cache Storage on Playwright's WebKit build (headless Chromium's Cache Storage put fails for a ~397 MiB body; this WebKit build's OPFS writable fails at any size — both measured, docs/evidence/S3/versions.json). Real-device Safari/iOS behavior is NOT_RUN (A27/A30).

Processing in S3 is the OCR + deterministic-cleanup pipeline; the model is downloaded, verified and cached but is CONSUMED by the S4 runtime (readCached() is the entry point). A14's zero-network claim covers the S3 pipeline end to end.

The streamed sha256 runs on the main thread between chunk reads (~23 MB/s measured): the download is hash-bound on fast links (~17 s for the pinned file over localhost) and the manager yields to the renderer every ~250 ms so the progress bar visibly moves; S4 moves the model runtime into a Worker and may revisit hashing.

A12's interrupted-download resume is proven with the local server destroying fresh requests mid-body (the wire log shows the Range resume); real flaky-network behavior (packet loss, proxies, captive portals) is not simulated beyond that.
Real installed-PWA sharing (A27), real-device offline/quota behavior (A27/A30), WebGPU (NOT_RUN on Linux) and arbitrary real-world screenshots remain outside what these headless-Linux runs prove.
The model file lives in gitignored .cache/models/ (never committed); CI downloads it once per job via scripts/fetch_model.mjs (~397 MB, seconds on the runner's network, far under its disk headroom).
